storage_extensions.usage: mmap order.bin as const int32_t*. After the join pipeline produces the set of candidate person_ids (as a bitset), scan order.bin sequentially: for k=0..N_name, let nrow=order[k]; pid=name_id[nrow]; if pid in candidate_pid_bitset, read name/name.{off,dat} at nrow — that string IS the MIN; break.

join_order.notes: Scan keyword/keyword.{off,dat} for keyword_eq; read keyword/id.bin at match -> target_kw_id.
Resolve country_code dict id from country_code.dict.{off,dat} (1-indexed). Scan company_name/country_code.bin (int16) and set bits in bitset of size (max_company_id+1)/8 ~ 30KB. Fits in L1.

join_order.build: movie_keyword aux CSR bucket for target_kw_id
join_order.notes: Use _idx/movie_keyword__keyword_id__{offsets,rowids}.bin (int32). Range [off[kw], off[kw+1]) gives mk rowids; read movie_keyword/movie_id.bin at each rowid. Sort + dedupe candidate_movies to improve probe locality.

For each candidate mid: (a) probe _idx/movie_companies__movie_id__offsets.bin (int32) and short-circuit if any movie_companies.company_id is in us_company_bitset; (b) on hit, probe _idx/cast_info__movie_id__offsets.bin (int32) for [lo,hi), read cast_info/person_id.bin[lo..hi), and set bit in candidate_pid_bitset (size = (max_name_id+1)/8 ~ 520 KB, fits in L2). No varlen name reads in this phase.

mmap column_versions/name.name.sortorder/order.bin (int32[N_name]). Iterate k=0..N_name-1: nrow=order[k]; pid=name_id[nrow]; if bit set in candidate_pid_bitset, read name/name.{off,dat} at nrow and that string IS MIN(n.name) (sortorder excludes empty strings by placing them at end). Expected first hit within tens of iterations given hit rate ~ |candidate_pids|/N_name.

optimization_notes: Iter 0 spent 46.5ms / 62ms in main_scan, dominated by ~258K random reads of name/name.{off,dat} for the running MIN aggregate. Root cause (Q2): name varlen reads are random-access into name.off (33 MB) and name.dat (60 MB), both far exceeding the 12 MB L3 — every name lookup is a cache miss chain. Fix (Category E, storage extension): built name.name.sortorder = int32[N_name] of row indices in lex-ascending name order (~644 ms one-time build, 16 MB file, reusable by any query needing MIN/MAX/top-K of name.name). The revised plan separates the join into two phases: (1) the join pipeline now writes survivors into a candidate_pid bitset (~520 KB, fits L2) instead of doing per-row name MIN updates; (2) MIN is computed by sequentially scanning sortorder and stopping at the first row whose person_id is in the bitset. With ~258K candidate pids out of 4.17M names, the expected first-hit position is ~16, so the MIN phase collapses from ~30 ms of random varlen access to a handful of sequential reads.
